ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          # No step-level DATASET here: a step env overrides the job env,
          # and a steps.* ref to the setup job's family step evaluates
          # EMPTY — harbor died with "Dataset  not found" (run 38126875911).
          # DATASET comes from the bench job's env block above
          # (needs.setup.outputs.dataset).
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # gh-1556 AC2: progress-watch is the bench default on EVERY
          # shard (#1392/#1430) — the gap-aware kill decision replaces
          # the retired byte-growth ladder that guillotined productive
          # trials (TB 2.0 Class C). FA_STALL_GAP_SEC pins the gh-1430
          # invariant (never below fa's 300s stream-idle watchdog +
          # margin — the REG in test_fa_agent_timeout.py reads the Dart
          # source and fails on drift); the abs ceiling is flat 3600s.
          # Removing these exports is the only way back to the legacy
          # ladder (its round-2 byte-for-byte REG stays green).
          # FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1 is required with the watch: without
          # it ProgressWatch degenerates to the flat base cap (the watch
          # only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # Pinned --job-name: one jobs/<name>/ dir per shard, so the summary
          # job's downloads cannot collide on harbor's timestamped default.
          # The family label keys results per dataset version (fa-4.0-*
          # matches the historical 4.0 names exactly).
          .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \

        # gh-1556 AC2: progress-watch (#1392/#1430) is the bench default —
        # every shard exports the watch knobs and the extension flag, so
        # the adapter's kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch.
        # Removing these exports is the only way back to the legacy
        # byte-growth ladder (its round-2 REG stays green).
        self.assertEqual(self._step_env("FA_STALL_GAP_SEC"), "360")
        self.assertEqual(self._step_env("FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC"), "3600")
        self.assertEqual(self._step_env("FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION"), "1")

        # The exported values must actually arm the watch: same env

                "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC": self._step_env(

            }

        # gh-1430 invariant: the bench stall-gap must stay above fa's

blocks.text:
Now I have a complete picture. Three code fixes:

1. **BLOCKING** (`bench/fa_agent_timeout.py`): watch branch of `effective_cap_sec` must honor `progress_extension` — return `base_sec` when off. RED test in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` `DeadlineEnvTest`.

2. **SUGGESTION** (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`): when unarmed, overlay `deadlineEpochMsEnvVar: ''` sentinel. Update the existing "unarmed: var absent" test to assert the scrub sentinel, and add a test that after `/timer clear` the var is present but empty (scrub). Check the existing test at line ~233.

3. **SUGGESTION** (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`): make the clip robust under `set -u` when the ceiling export is removed:
```bash
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
```
Wait — the suggested form. Current line:
```bash
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
```
The reviewer suggests: `export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"` — hmm, that alone would default the ceiling to base×4 but lose the min() clip when the ceiling IS set. Reading again: "(i.e. clip against the step-env ceiling when present, otherwise default the ceiling to base × 4 — precisely what the legacy ladder would have used.)" So the form is: if ceiling set, clip (min), else default to base×4. So:

```bash
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
```

Or combine. The simplest robust form preserving both semantics:

```bash
ceiling="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( ceiling < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? ceiling : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
```

But the reviewer's suggested snippet is the single-line `${VAR:-default}`. Actually, the reviewer's code is:

```bash
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
```

That would REPLACE the clip... no wait. Let me re-read: "the graceful form costs nothing and matches the pre-PR ladder semantics exactly: `export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"` (i.e. clip against the step-env ceiling when present, otherwise default the ceiling to `base × 4` — precisely what the legacy ladder would have used.)"

Hmm, but that single line alone doesn't clip when the ceiling is present (3600 < 600*4=2400 would need min → 2400). E.g., AGENT_TIMEOUT=600, ceiling=3600 present → line leaves 3600, but the clip intent is min(3600, 2400)=2400. So the reviewer probably means to add the `:-` default BEFORE the existing clip line, i.e.:

```bash
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
```

Hmm wait, but under `set -u`, if FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC is unset, `${VAR:-default}` works fine (that's the point). Then the second line re-exports with the min clip. Actually the first line with `:-` sets it to base×4 when unset; the second line then computes min(base×4, base×4) = base×4. When set: first line keeps it, second clips. That's exactly "clip against the step-env ceiling when present, otherwise default the ceiling to base×4".

Simpler two-in-one:
```bash
ceiling="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( ceiling < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? ceiling : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
```

But the existing REG test `test_agent_timeout_input_clips_the_watch_ceiling` asserts the string `"FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4"` is present. Keep that string. I'll use the two-line form, or a single line that keeps that substring:

```bash
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( ${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))} < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? ${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))} : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
```

That's ugly. Two lines is cleaner. But `set -u` with the ternary referencing the var after the default export line is fine.

Actually simplest, keeping the existing clip line untouched and adding one line before it:

```bash
# The ceiling export is individually removable (the escape hatch back
# to the legacy ladder) — under set -u a missing ceiling must default
```

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

`LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).

`LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after

  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume

Now I have a complete picture. Three code fixes:

1. **BLOCKING** (`bench/fa_agent_timeout.py`): watch branch of `effective_cap_sec` must honor `progress_extension` — return `base_sec` when off. RED test in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` `DeadlineEnvTest`.

2. **SUGGESTION** (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`): when unarmed, overlay `deadlineEpochMsEnvVar: ''` sentinel. Update the existing "unarmed: var absent" test to assert the scrub sentinel, and add a test that after `/timer clear` the var is present but empty (scrub). Check the existing test at line ~233.

3. **SUGGESTION** (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`): make the clip robust under `set -u` when the ceiling export is removed:
```bash
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
```
Wait — the suggested form. Current line:
```bash
export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
```
The reviewer suggests: `export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"` — hmm, that alone would default the ceiling to base×4 but lose the min() clip when the ceiling IS set. Reading again: "(i.e. clip against the step-env ceiling when present, otherwise default the ceiling to base × 4 — precisely what the legacy ladder would have used.)" # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

`LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

blocks.text:
`LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap

blocks.text:
`LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

356:  keep-alive pool is test-exonerated for every watchdog-window class).

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"

          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null

          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # Pinned --job-name: one jobs/<name>/ dir per shard, so the summary
          # job's downloads cannot collide on harbor's timestamped default.
          # The family label keys results per dataset version (fa-4.0-*
          # matches the historical 4.0 names exactly).
          .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
            -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
            --job-name "fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${{ matrix.kind }}-${{ matrix.i }}" -o jobs \
            "${args[@]}"

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |

          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT

          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"

          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +

      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"

          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # Pinned --job-name: one jobs/<name>/ dir per shard, so the summary
          # job's downloads cannot collide on harbor's timestamped default.
          # The family label keys results per dataset version (fa-4.0-*
          # matches the historical 4.0 names exactly).
          .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
            -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
            --job-name "fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${{ matrix.kind }}-${{ matrix.i }}" -o jobs \
            "${args[@]}"

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"

# Rework: gh-1556 re-review threads (PR #1559)

All 5 open review threads are addressed (1 blocking, 2 minor/suggestion pairs, 1 new suggestion) — threads 6+9 by one change, threads 8+10 by one change, thread 11 by the workflow guard. Machine-verdict / consumption-audit comments are not threaded review feedback and get no reply.

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (thread 9, AC7)**: `effective_cap_sec` promised the 3600s abs ceiling in watch mode even with `progress_extension` off — but `ProgressWatch` then kills at the flat `base_sec`, so the exported deadline lied by ~52–58 min and every wrap-up steer fired after the kill. Workflow-reachable via the rework's own `progress-extension: false` → `unset` path.
- 💡 **Thread 8/10**: `/timer clear` could not scrub a host-exported `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` from bash children — the overlay only added keys, and `LocalShell` merges the overlay over `Platform.environment`.
- 💡 **Thread 11 (new, on the rework)**: the `agent-timeout` clip died under `set -u` if the ceiling export was removed while `agent-timeout` stayed set — the escape hatch ("remove the watch exports") was not individually load-bearing-safe.

## Approach

1. **Watch-branch cap honors the extension (threads 6+9)** — `effective_cap_sec` in `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` now returns `base_sec` when `progress_extension` is off, `watch_abs_ceiling_sec` when on (the exact fix prescribed in the thread, with the test-budget fold preserved on both legs). The docstring states the «never lie about the clock» invariant explicitly. With the extension off the deadline derives from the same cap `ProgressWatch.__post_init__` pins `kill_at` to.
2. **Empty-string scrub sentinel (threads 8+10)** — `_sessionEnvVars` in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` overlays `deadlineEpochMsEnvVar: ''` when unarmed instead of omitting the key. `LocalShell` merges `options.env` over `Platform.environment`, so the sentinel scrubs a stale host export from every bash exec; `resolveSessionDeadline`'s `raw.isNotEmpty` check makes a scrubbed child resolve to unarmed exactly like a host with no export.
3. **`set -u` guard on the clip (thread 11)** — the shard run script now defaults the ceiling before clipping: `export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"` above the existing min-clip line. Ceiling export removed → defaults to base × 4 (exactly the legacy-ladder ceiling); present → clip semantics unchanged.

## Files Modified

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` — watch branch of `effective_cap_sec` honors `progress_extension`; docstring updated.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` — new REG `test_watch_mode_without_extension_deadline_is_base_minus_margin` in `DeadlineEnvTest` (pins `ProgressWatch.kill_at == base_sec`, `effective_cap_sec == base_sec`, `deadline_env_from → now + 240_000`).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `_sessionEnvVars` unarmed sentinel + doc comment.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart` — «unarmed: the var rides as an empty scrub sentinel» (replaces the old absent-key test) + «clear: the overlay scrubs a previously-armed value».
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` — `:-` ceiling default above the clip (individually-removable exports safe under `set -euo pipefail`).
- `bench/harbor_fa/test_bench_harbor_workflow.py` — new REG `test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed` pinning the guard.

## Test Coverage

- **RED first (TDD)**: the watch-cap REG failed pre-fix (`3600.0 != 360.0`); the scrub-sentinel tests failed pre-fix (`<null>` / absent key); the workflow guard REG failed pre-fix — all green after.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` — **357 ok** (356 + 1 new; 16 skips pre-existing).
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` — **81 ok** (80 + 1 new).
- Shell semantics verified under `set -euo pipefail`: ceiling removed + `AGENT_TIMEOUT=600` → 2400; ceiling 3600 + 600 → 2400; ceiling 3600 + 1200 → 3600.
- `dart test test/session_deadline_test.dart test/agent/session_deadline_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_test.dart` — **103/103 green**; `test/env/session_vars_execution_env_test.dart` + `test/hosts/host_agent_wiring_test.dart` — 32/32 green.
- `dart analyze` on changed Dart files — clean (1 pre-existing info-level lint in the test file, untouched by this rework).
- `crap4dart analyze` — **Max CRAP: 0.00 — OK (threshold 12.00)**; `crap4dart check --baseline` — 3 passed, 1 pre-existing duplication warn on untouched files.
- Full `dart test` suite: <!-- FILLED AFTER RUN -->

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)

{"content":"# Rework: gh-1556 re-review threads (PR #1559)

All 5 open review threads are addressed (1 blocking, 2 minor/suggestion pairs, 1 new suggestion) — threads 6+9 by one change, threads 8+10 by one change, thread 11 by the workflow guard. Machine-verdict / consumption-audit comments are not threaded review feedback and get no reply.

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (thread 9, AC7)**: `effective_cap_sec` promised the 3600s abs ceiling in watch mode even with `progress_extension` off — but `ProgressWatch` then kills at the flat `base_sec`, so the exported deadline lied by ~52–58 min and every wrap-up steer fired after the kill. Workflow-reachable via the rework's own `progress-extension: false` → `unset` path.
- 💡 **Thread 8/10**: `/timer clear` could not scrub a host-exported `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` from bash children — the overlay only added keys, and `LocalShell` merges the overlay over `Platform.environment`.
- 💡 **Thread 11 (new, on the rework)**: the `agent-timeout` clip died under `set -u` if the ceiling export was removed while `agent-timeout` stayed set — the escape hatch ("remove the watch exports") was not individually load-bearing-safe.

## Approach

1. **Watch-branch cap honors the extension (threads 6+9)** — `effective_cap_sec` in `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` now returns `base_sec` when `progress_extension` is off, `watch_abs_ceiling_sec` when on (the exact fix prescribed in the thread, with the test-budget fold preserved on both legs). The docstring states the «never lie about the clock» invariant explicitly. With the extension off the deadline derives from the same cap `ProgressWatch.__post_init__` pins `kill_at` to.
2. **Empty-string scrub sentinel (threads 8+10)** — `_sessionEnvVars` in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` overlays `deadlineEpochMsEnvVar: ''` when unarmed instead of omitting the key. `LocalShell` merges `options.env` over `Platform.environment`, so the sentinel scrubs a stale host export from every bash exec; `resolveSessionDeadline`'s `raw.isNotEmpty` check makes a scrubbed child resolve to unarmed exactly like a host with no export.
3. **`set -u` guard on the clip (thread 11)** — the shard run script now defaults the ceiling before clipping: `export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"` above the existing min-clip line. Ceiling export removed → defaults to base × 4 (exactly the legacy-ladder ceiling); present → clip semantics unchanged.

## Files Modified

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` — watch branch of `effective_cap_sec` honors `progress_extension`; docstring updated.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` — new REG `test_watch_mode_without_extension_deadline_is_base_minus_margin` in `DeadlineEnvTest` (pins `ProgressWatch.kill_at == base_sec`, `effective_cap_sec == base_sec`, `deadline_env_from → now + 240_000`).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `_sessionEnvVars` unarmed sentinel + doc comment.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart` — «unarmed: the var rides as an empty scrub sentinel» (replaces the old absent-key test) + «clear: the overlay scrubs a previously-armed value».
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` — `:-` ceiling default above the clip (individually-removable exports safe under `set -euo pipefail`).
- `bench/harbor_fa/test_bench_harbor_workflow.py` — new REG `test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed` pinning the guard.

## Test Coverage

- **RED first (TDD)**: the watch-cap REG failed pre-fix (`3600.0 != 360.0`); the scrub-sentinel tests failed pre-fix (`<null>` / absent key); the workflow guard REG failed pre-fix — all green after.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` — **357 ok** (356 + 1 new; 16 skips pre-existing).
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` — **81 ok** (80 + 1 new).
- Shell semantics verified under `set -euo pipefail`: ceiling removed + `AGENT_TIMEOUT=600` → 2400; ceiling 3600 + 600 → 2400; ceiling 3600 + 1200 → 3600.
- `dart test test/session_deadline_test.dart test/agent/session_deadline_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_test.dart` — **103/103 green**; `test/env/session_vars_execution_env_test.dart` + `test/hosts/host_agent_wiring_test.dart` — 32/32 green.
- `dart analyze` on changed Dart files — clean (1 pre-existing info-level lint in the test file, untouched by this rework).
- `crap4dart analyze` — **Max CRAP: 0.00 — OK (threshold 12.00)**; `crap4dart check --baseline` — 3 passed, 1 pre-existing duplication warn on untouched files.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"

{"content":"# Rework: gh-1556 re-review threads (PR #1559)

All 5 open review threads are addressed (1 blocking, 2 minor/suggestion pairs, 1 new suggestion) — threads 6+9 by one change, threads 8+10 by one change, thread 11 by the workflow guard. Machine-verdict / consumption-audit comments are not threaded review feedback and get no reply.

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (thread 9, AC7)**: `effective_cap_sec` promised the 3600s abs ceiling in watch mode even with `progress_extension` off — but `ProgressWatch` then kills at the flat `base_sec`, so the exported deadline lied by ~52–58 min and every wrap-up steer fired after the kill. Workflow-reachable via the rework's own `progress-extension: false` → `unset` path.
- 💡 **Thread 8/10**: `/timer clear` could not scrub a host-exported `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` from bash children — the overlay only added keys, and `LocalShell` merges the overlay over `Platform.environment`.
- 💡 **Thread 11 (new, on the rework)**: the `agent-timeout` clip died under `set -u` if the ceiling export was removed while `agent-timeout` stayed set — the escape hatch ("remove the watch exports") was not individually load-bearing-safe.

## Approach

1. **Watch-branch cap honors the extension (threads 6+9)** — `effective_cap_sec` in `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` now returns `base_sec` when `progress_extension` is off, `watch_abs_ceiling_sec` when on (the exact fix prescribed in the thread, with the test-budget fold preserved on both legs). The docstring states the «never lie about the clock» invariant explicitly. With the extension off the deadline derives from the same cap `ProgressWatch.__post_init__` pins `kill_at` to.
2. **Empty-string scrub sentinel (threads 8+10)** — `_sessionEnvVars` in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` overlays `deadlineEpochMsEnvVar: ''` when unarmed instead of omitting the key. `LocalShell` merges `options.env` over `Platform.environment`, so the sentinel scrubs a stale host export from every bash exec; `resolveSessionDeadline`'s `raw.isNotEmpty` check makes a scrubbed child resolve to unarmed exactly like a host with no export.
3. **`set -u` guard on the clip (thread 11)** — the shard run script now defaults the ceiling before clipping: `export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"` above the existing min-clip line. Ceiling export removed → defaults to base × 4 (exactly the legacy-ladder ceiling); present → clip semantics unchanged.

## Files Modified

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` — watch branch of `effective_cap_sec` honors `progress_extension`; docstring updated.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` — new REG `test_watch_mode_without_extension_deadline_is_base_minus_margin` in `DeadlineEnvTest` (pins `ProgressWatch.kill_at == base_sec`, `effective_cap_sec == base_sec`, `deadline_env_from → now + 240_000`).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `_sessionEnvVars` unarmed sentinel + doc comment.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart` — «unarmed: the var rides as an empty scrub sentinel» (replaces the old absent-key test) + «clear: the overlay scrubs a previously-armed value».
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` — `:-` ceiling default above the clip (individually-removable exports safe under `set -euo pipefail`).
- `bench/harbor_fa/test_bench_harbor_workflow.py` — new REG `test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed` pinning the guard.

## Test Coverage

- **RED first (TDD)**: the watch-cap REG failed pre-fix (`3600.0 != 360.0`); the scrub-sentinel tests failed pre-fix (`<null>` / absent key); the workflow guard REG failed pre-fix — all green after.

{"content":"# Rework: gh-1556 re-review threads (PR #1559)

All 5 open review threads are addressed (1 blocking, 2 minor/suggestion pairs, 1 new suggestion) — threads 6+9 by one change, threads 8+10 by one change, thread 11 by the workflow guard. Machine-verdict / consumption-audit comments are not threaded review feedback and get no reply.

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (thread 9, AC7)**: `effective_cap_sec` promised the 3600s abs ceiling in watch mode even with `progress_extension` off — but `ProgressWatch` then kills at the flat `base_sec`, so the exported deadline lied by ~52–58 min and every wrap-up steer fired after the kill. Workflow-reachable via the rework's own `progress-extension: false` → `unset` path.
- 💡 **Thread 8/10**: `/timer clear` could not scrub a host-exported `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` from bash children — the overlay only added keys, and `LocalShell` merges the overlay over `Platform.environment`.
- 💡 **Thread 11 (new, on the rework)**: the `agent-timeout` clip died under `set -u` if the ceiling export was removed while `agent-timeout` stayed set — the escape hatch ("remove the watch exports") was not individually load-bearing-safe.

## Approach

1. **Watch-branch cap honors the extension (threads 6+9)** — `effective_cap_sec` in `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` now returns `base_sec` when `progress_extension` is off, `watch_abs_ceiling_sec` when on (the exact fix prescribed in the thread, with the test-budget fold preserved on both legs). The docstring states the «never lie about the clock» invariant explicitly. With the extension off the deadline derives from the same cap `ProgressWatch.__post_init__` pins `kill_at` to.
2. **Empty-string scrub sentinel (threads 8+10)** — `_sessionEnvVars` in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` overlays `deadlineEpochMsEnvVar: ''` when unarmed instead of omitting the key. `LocalShell` merges `options.env` over `Platform.environment`, so the sentinel scrubs a stale host export from every bash exec; `resolveSessionDeadline`'s `raw.isNotEmpty` check makes a scrubbed child resolve to unarmed exactly like a host with no export.
3. **`set -u` guard on the clip (thread 11)** — the shard run script now defaults the ceiling before clipping: `export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"` above the existing min-clip line. Ceiling export removed → defaults to base × 4 (exactly the legacy-ladder ceiling); present → clip semantics unchanged.

## Files Modified

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` — watch branch of `effective_cap_sec` honors `progress_extension`; docstring updated.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` — new REG `test_watch_mode_without_extension_deadline_is_base_minus_margin` in `DeadlineEnvTest` (pins `ProgressWatch.kill_at == base_sec`, `effective_cap_sec == base_sec`, `deadline_env_from → now + 240_000`).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `_sessionEnvVars` unarmed sentinel + doc comment.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart` — «unarmed: the var rides as an empty scrub sentinel» (replaces the old absent-key test) + «clear: the overlay scrubs a previously-armed value».
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` — `:-` ceiling default above the clip (individually-removable exports safe under `set -euo pipefail`).
- `bench/harbor_fa/test_bench_harbor_workflow.py` — new REG `test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed` pinning the guard.

## Test Coverage

- **RED first (TDD)**: the watch-cap REG failed pre-fix (`3600.0 != 360.0`); the scrub-sentinel tests failed pre-fix (`<null>` / absent key); the workflow guard REG failed pre-fix — all green after.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` — **357 ok** (356 + 1 new; 16 skips pre-existing).
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` — **81 ok** (80 + 1 new).

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +

      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"

{"content":"# Rework: gh-1556 re-review threads (PR #1559)

All 5 open review threads are addressed (1 blocking, 2 minor/suggestion pairs, 1 new suggestion) — threads 6+9 by one change, threads 8+10 by one change, thread 11 by the workflow guard. Machine-verdict / consumption-audit comments are not threaded review feedback and get no reply.

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (thread 9, AC7)**: `effective_cap_sec` promised the 3600s abs ceiling in watch mode even with `progress_extension` off — but `ProgressWatch` then kills at the flat `base_sec`, so the exported deadline lied by ~52–58 min and every wrap-up steer fired after the kill. Workflow-reachable via the rework's own `progress-extension: false` → `unset` path.
- 💡 **Thread 8/10**: `/timer clear` could not scrub a host-exported `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` from bash children — the overlay only added keys, and `LocalShell` merges the overlay over `Platform.environment`.
- 💡 **Thread 11 (new, on the rework)**: the `agent-timeout` clip died under `set -u` if the ceiling export was removed while `agent-timeout` stayed set — the escape hatch ("remove the watch exports") was not individually load-bearing-safe.

## Approach

1. **Watch-branch cap honors the extension (threads 6+9)** — `effective_cap_sec` in `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` now returns `base_sec` when `progress_extension` is off, `watch_abs_ceiling_sec` when on (the exact fix prescribed in the thread, with the test-budget fold preserved on both legs). The docstring states the «never lie about the clock» invariant explicitly. With the extension off the deadline derives from the same cap `ProgressWatch.__post_init__` pins `kill_at` to.
2. **Empty-string scrub sentinel (threads 8+10)** — `_sessionEnvVars` in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` overlays `deadlineEpochMsEnvVar: ''` when unarmed instead of omitting the key. `LocalShell` merges `options.env` over `Platform.environment`, so the sentinel scrubs a stale host export from every bash exec; `resolveSessionDeadline`'s `raw.isNotEmpty` check makes a scrubbed child resolve to unarmed exactly like a host with no export.
3. **`set -u` guard on the clip (thread 11)** — the shard run script now defaults the ceiling before clipping: `export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"` above the existing min-clip line. Ceiling export removed → defaults to base × 4 (exactly the legacy-ladder ceiling); present → clip semantics unchanged.

## Files Modified

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` — watch branch of `effective_cap_sec` honors `progress_extension`; docstring updated.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` — new REG `test_watch_mode_without_extension_deadline_is_base_minus_margin` in `DeadlineEnvTest` (pins `ProgressWatch.kill_at == base_sec`, `effective_cap_sec == base_sec`, `deadline_env_from → now + 240_000`).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `_sessionEnvVars` unarmed sentinel + doc comment.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart` — «unarmed: the var rides as an empty scrub sentinel» (replaces the old absent-key test) + «clear: the overlay scrubs a previously-armed value».
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` — `:-` ceiling default above the clip (individually-removable exports safe under `set -euo pipefail`).
- `bench/harbor_fa/test_bench_harbor_workflow.py` — new REG `test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed` pinning the guard.

## Test Coverage

- **RED first (TDD)**: the watch-cap REG failed pre-fix (`3600.0 != 360.0`); the scrub-sentinel tests failed pre-fix (`<null>` / absent key); the workflow guard REG failed pre-fix — all green after.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` — **357 ok** (356 + 1 new; 16 skips pre-existing).
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` — **81 ok** (80 + 1 new).
- Shell semantics verified under `set -euo pipefail`: ceiling removed + `AGENT_TIMEOUT=600` → 2400; ceiling 3600 + 600 → 2400; ceiling 3600 + 1200 → 3600.
- `dart test test/session_deadline_test.dart test/agent/session_deadline_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_test.dart` — **103/103 green**; `test/env/session_vars_execution_env_test.dart` + `test/hosts/host_agent_wiring_test.dart` — 32/32 green.
- `dart analyze` on changed Dart files — clean (1 pre-existing info-level lint in the test file, untouched by this rework).
- `crap4dart analyze` — **Max CRAP: 0.00 — OK (threshold 12.00)**; `crap4dart check --baseline` — 3 passed, 1 pre-existing duplication warn on untouched files.

{"content":"# Rework: gh-1556 re-review threads (PR #1559)

All 5 open review threads are addressed (1 blocking, 2 minor/suggestion pairs, 1 new suggestion) — threads 6+9 by one change, threads 8+10 by one change, thread 11 by the workflow guard. Machine-verdict / consumption-audit comments are not threaded review feedback and get no reply.

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (thread 9, AC7)**: `effective_cap_sec` promised the 3600s abs ceiling in watch mode even with `progress_extension` off — but `ProgressWatch` then kills at the flat `base_sec`, so the exported deadline lied by ~52–58 min and every wrap-up steer fired after the kill. Workflow-reachable via the rework's own `progress-extension: false` → `unset` path.
- 💡 **Thread 8/10**: `/timer clear` could not scrub a host-exported `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` from bash children — the overlay only added keys, and `LocalShell` merges the overlay over `Platform.environment`.
- 💡 **Thread 11 (new, on the rework)**: the `agent-timeout` clip died under `set -u` if the ceiling export was removed while `agent-timeout` stayed set — the escape hatch ("remove the watch exports") was not individually load-bearing-safe.

## Approach

1. **Watch-branch cap honors the extension (threads 6+9)** — `effective_cap_sec` in `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` now returns `base_sec` when `progress_extension` is off, `watch_abs_ceiling_sec` when on (the exact fix prescribed in the thread, with the test-budget fold preserved on both legs). The docstring states the «never lie about the clock» invariant explicitly. With the extension off the deadline derives from the same cap `ProgressWatch.__post_init__` pins `kill_at` to.
2. **Empty-string scrub sentinel (threads 8+10)** — `_sessionEnvVars` in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` overlays `deadlineEpochMsEnvVar: ''` when unarmed instead of omitting the key. `LocalShell` merges `options.env` over `Platform.environment`, so the sentinel scrubs a stale host export from every bash exec; `resolveSessionDeadline`'s `raw.isNotEmpty` check makes a scrubbed child resolve to unarmed exactly like a host with no export.
3. **`set -u` guard on the clip (thread 11)** — the shard run script now defaults the ceiling before clipping: `export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"` above the existing min-clip line. Ceiling export removed → defaults to base × 4 (exactly the legacy-ladder ceiling); present → clip semantics unchanged.

## Files Modified

- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` — watch branch of `effective_cap_sec` honors `progress_extension`; docstring updated.
- `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` — new REG `test_watch_mode_without_extension_deadline_is_base_minus_margin` in `DeadlineEnvTest` (pins `ProgressWatch.kill_at == base_sec`, `effective_cap_sec == base_sec`, `deadline_env_from → now + 240_000`).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `_sessionEnvVars` unarmed sentinel + doc comment.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart` — «unarmed: the var rides as an empty scrub sentinel» (replaces the old absent-key test) + «clear: the overlay scrubs a previously-armed value».
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` — `:-` ceiling default above the clip (individually-removable exports safe under `set -euo pipefail`).
- `bench/harbor_fa/test_bench_harbor_workflow.py` — new REG `test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed` pinning the guard.

## Test Coverage

- **RED first (TDD)**: the watch-cap REG failed pre-fix (`3600.0 != 360.0`); the scrub-sentinel tests failed pre-fix (`<null>` / absent key); the workflow guard REG failed pre-fix — all green after.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` — **357 ok** (356 + 1 new; 16 skips pre-existing).
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` — **81 ok** (80 + 1 new).
- Shell semantics verified under `set -euo pipefail`: ceiling removed + `AGENT_TIMEOUT=600` → 2400; ceiling 3600 + 600 → 2400; ceiling 3600 + 1200 → 3600.
- `dart test test/session_deadline_test.dart test/agent/session_deadline_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_test.dart` — **103/103 green**; `test/env/session_vars_execution_env_test.dart` + `test/hosts/host_agent_wiring_test.dart` — 32/32 green.
- `dart analyze` on changed Dart files — clean (1 pre-existing info-level lint in the test file, untouched by this rework).
- `crap4dart analyze` — **Max CRAP: 0.00 — OK (threshold 12.00)**; `crap4dart check --baseline` — 3 passed, 1 pre-existing duplication warn on untouched files.

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"

          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
